sources.facts: Official current description is based on boundary observations/heritage photographs, not interior survey. Single-storey rectangular timber-framed observatory on low timber stumps; weatherboards; north/east verandas now enclosed with casement windows; hipped corrugated fibre-cement roof with north/east/west louvred gablets and entry gable, no eaves gutters; southwest shed. Instruments: Stevenson screen on approximately1.2m steel frame, northern concrete strip/cut-off pipes, eastern clay temperature-pit caps approximately0.3m above ground, telescope removed leaving memorial marker, sundial stand west of screen. No gallery pixels used.

Public QRA vector data combines open building data and automatically extracted LiDAR footprints. Use geometry/relative roof controls only; automated floor/class/height attributes are approximate, not surveyed identity or construction evidence.

Individually inspected exact1432x1003 native crop of the1935 Courier-Mail opening-day photograph. Broad low timber-stumped observatory with open north/east return veranda, close vertical battens/posts, hipped corrugated roof with three louvred gablets and a small entry gable near the front-right, stairs and weatherboard inner walls. It establishes original roof/post proportions, not present enclosed-veranda casement details or all-side coverage. People/cars/bunting/trees excluded. Current enclosure, southwest shed and surviving instruments follow official primary heritage text, with hidden sections estimated. Trove source article returned a bot-check page and was not bypassed; exact native publication citation/PD-Australia/date/bytes and NLA first-party photograph-expiration guidance are bound.
